newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teachers strike paralyses Palestinian schools.
newsitem.headline: Teachers strike paralyses Palestinian schools.

text.p: Palestinian teachers demanding higher pay paralysed public sector schools in the West Bank on Monday in the first labour dispute involving Palestinian Authority employees.

Up to 18,000 teachers have been on strike since Saturday to protest against a Palestinian Education Ministry decision to suspend 19 teachers and bring them before a disciplinary committee for leading a fight to double salaries.
The ministry said the decision was cancelled and appealed to teachers to return to work.
Teachers were due to meet later in the day to discuss continuing the strike, which began with partial protests last month.
About 20,000 school teachers are on the Palestinian Authority's payroll in the West Bank. Teachers say that average monthly pay is about $400, barely enough to cover basic expenses.
Education Minister Yasser Amr told Voice of Palestine radio the ministry had offered pay rises of up to 15 percent despite budget constraints.

The Palestinian Authority took charge of most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank under a 1993 self-rule deal. The Palestinian Authority provides free education to Palestinians until high school.
